title: The coefficient comparisons commute with inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E\subseteq\Qlb$ with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Use the condensed coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and their pulled-back ring sheaves $\Lambda_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In particular, $E_Z$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z}$ are [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] and [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring]. The finite-subextension cocone is [def-sfb-qlbar-x-cocone].

Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and let
$\alpha_f\colon f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X$ be the canonical isomorphism
induced by $p_Y\circ f=p_X$ ([sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]), for
$\Lambda=\underline{\cO_E},\underline E,\underline{\Qlb}$. Index the integral system by $n\ge1$. Then, under $\alpha_f$ and the
canonical isomorphisms $f^{-1}(T_Y)\cong T_X$ for constant sheaves:

1. $f^{-1}$ of the isomorphism $\cO_{E,Y}\cong\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$ is the
   isomorphism $\cO_{E,X}\cong\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$
   ([det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]); in particular $f^{-1}$ carries the
   limit $\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$ to $\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$;
2. $f^{-1}$ of $E_Y\cong\cO_{E,Y}[1/\ell]$ is $E_X\cong\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]$
   ([det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]);
3. $f^{-1}$ of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Y}\cong\varinjlim_EE_Y$ is
   $\QbarX\cong\varinjlim_EE_X$.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized integral comparison isomorphisms eX and eY and the finite profinite cones from sfb_integral_coefficient_limit. Package its normalization data as SfbIntegralComparison. The supplied pointwise quotient formulas show that jX followed by the nth profinite cone leg equals jY followed by its nth leg, by extensionality of continuous maps.

proof.text: For each n, apply [lem-sfb-finite-reduction-pullback] to rZ = eZ followed by the nth completed-coefficient projection, using the common profinite quotient map. The mate hypotheses are exactly the normalization equations supplied by sfb_integral_coefficient_limit. This proves compatibility of every finite reduction with alpha_f.

proof.text: Construct the ring-compatible isomorphism c by conjugating alpha_f with eY and eX inside the category of monoid objects, then forget to abelian sheaves. Functoriality and inverse cancellation give the comparison square, and the monoid-object morphisms give IsMonHom for both directions. Cancel f^*eY in the preceding finite-reduction equation to obtain every projection equation for c. The canonical finite pullback comparisons form a natural isomorphism of towers: their successor naturality is naturality of the constant/forgetful and constant-pullback natural isomorphisms. Build the tower transformation with NatTrans.ofOpSequence. Forgetting rings to abelian sheaves preserves this limit, as checked after the limit-reflecting sheaf inclusion by pointwise limit preservation. Transport that limiting cone along the diagram isomorphism and c, using the proved projection equations. This proves the asserted preservation of this particular integral limit.

source.place: second paragraph, finite quotient maps and the adjunction-mate check (parent proof Steps 1--2)

proof.text: For (2), apply padicIntegers_invertEll on X and Y to the two given module-colimit representatives. It supplies ring isomorphisms eX and eY identifying every leg with the fraction cocone. At m=0 this gives the two required integral inclusions. Define the comparison c by conjugating coefficientPullbackIso for E with eY and the inverse of eX. Associativity and inverse cancellation give the required isomorphism square. Naturality of upperStarFromPointComp for the integral inclusion proves the leg equation at m=0. Every cocone over the multiplication-by-ell sequence satisfies ell times leg(m+1) = leg(m). The underlying abelian inverse image is additive, so both sides of the desired leg equation satisfy this recurrence after composition with eX. Multiplication by ell on E_X has the inverse t supplied by padicIntegers_invertEll; consequently equality at m implies equality at m+1 by composing with t. Induction proves equality for every m. Finally cancel the underlying isomorphism eX. All ring comparisons are composites of the supplied ring isomorphisms; no module-pullback construction or extra preservation theorem is required.

proof.text: Apply the published isColimitPadicAlgClRingObjCocone and preservation of colimits by the left adjoint abelian inverse image. For each inclusion leg, use naturality of upperStarFromPointComp. The generic ringComparisonNaturality helper computes the underlying map of the monoidal ring comparison before specializing to sheaves. This proves both conjuncts of the algebraic-closure clause.

lean.statement: theorem sfb_integral_comparison_pullback (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : ∃ (eX : (coefficientRing X (sfbCondensedIntegers l (ULift.{u} E.1))).X ≅ sfbCompletedIntegersAb l (ULift.{u} E.1) X) (eY : (coefficientRing Y (sfbCondensedIntegers l (ULift.{u} E.1))).X ≅ sfbCompletedIntegersAb l (ULift.{u} E.1) Y), SfbIntegralComparison l (ULift.{u} E.1) X eX ∧ SfbIntegralComparison l (ULift.{u} E.1) Y eY ∧ ∃ c : (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].obj (sfbCompletedIntegersAb l (ULift.{u} E.1) Y) ≅ sfbCompletedIntegersAb l (ULift.{u} E.1) X, (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].mapIso eY ≪≫ c = (upperStarFromPointComp f).app (sfbCondensedIntegers l (ULift.{u} E.1)).X ≪≫ eX ∧ IsMonHom c.hom ∧ IsMonHom c.inv ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].map ((sheafCompose _ (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).map (limit.π (integralCoefficientSheafSystem l (ULift.{u} E.1) Y) (op n))) ≫ (sfbFiniteCoefficientPullbackIso l (ULift.{u} E.1) f n).hom = c.hom ≫ (sheafCompose _ (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).map (limit.π (integralCoefficientSheafSystem l (ULift.{u} E.1) X) (op n))) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit ((f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].mapCone ((sheafCompose _ (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).mapCone (limit.cone (integralCoefficientSheafSystem l (ULift.{u} E.1) Y)))))
lean.note: Clauses 1, 2 and 3 are the three listed comparison theorems. The integral clause uses the canonical universe lift of the fixed finite subextension and the dependency’s adjunction-mate normalization; it identifies the comparison by every finite projection and states preservation of that particular limit. The localization clause is independent of the choice of module-colimit representatives, uses ring isomorphisms normalized at the integral inclusion, and checks every fraction leg. The algebraic-closure clause uses the recorded cocone, states its inverse image is colimiting, and identifies its canonical ring comparison by all inclusion legs. The three definition helpers only express the canonical constant-sheaf transport and the integral dependency’s normalization. E6: the two canonical finite constant-sheaf isomorphisms are now defined verbatim in ProEtaleFiniteReductionPullback and publicly re-exported here; the normalization predicate remains here.
